whoami.purpose: Identify the signed-in user and the groups they belong to, including their own profile and per-group settings. Read at startup and by ~40 call sites as the ambient identity context.
whoami.reason: Genuine requirement: every backend needs a 'who am I and what may I see' operation. But this is the most SSB-shaped accessor in the corpus (feedId, recps, authors/intervals, tombstone, originalAuthor) and 40 files depend on it. The contract should express it as identity plus group membership, not as a feed identity plus recipient lists. First thing any adapter must satisfy, and the place the permission model gets decided.

getPerson.purpose: Fetch a person's full profile together with their whakapapa links and the authors who contributed to the record - the read behind opening a person in the tree.
getPerson.reason: Core whakapapa read; absorbs getPersonFull. The authors/intervals selection is SSB provenance and should be triaged separately from the profile itself - a contract that bakes author intervals into every person read will not port cleanly.

getPersonMinimal.purpose: Display a person in lists, pickers and submission previews - name, gender, avatar, life dates, birth order, and whether the record is tombstoned.
getPersonMinimal.reason: Same record at a narrower projection. Arbitrary field selection is a GraphQL affordance, not a frontend requirement - a Holochain zome call or nostr event returns a whole record either way. Merging costs some over-fetch on list views; keeping four projections costs four operations per entity in every adapter. If list views later prove to need a lean shape, reintroduce it as an explicit contract-level summary type, not an ad-hoc selection.

getPersonFull.purpose: Fetch a person's profile plus the kaitiaki adminProfile that may override group-profile details.
getPersonFull.reason: Differs from getPerson only by projection and the adminProfile overlay, and has one call site. The adminProfile override is a real requirement and must survive the merge - it governs whose version of a record you see, which is a permissions question every adapter has to answer.

getPersonCustomFields.purpose: Read a person's tribe-defined custom fields - the key/value pairs an iwi or hapu adds beyond the standard profile schema.
getPersonCustomFields.reason: Not a projection of getPerson: custom fields are a distinct extensibility concern with their own permission scope, and the query selects recps directly. Keeping it separate lets the contract express who may see which custom fields without entangling the base profile read. The recps flag here is direct, not inherited - this is where tribal field-level privacy actually lives.

savePerson.purpose: Create or update a person profile.
savePerson.reason: Irreducible write, no SSB flags. The contract question is not whether to keep it but what it returns: Apollo yields a bare id, Holochain an action hash, nostr an event id with per-relay acknowledgement. Write-acknowledgement shape is a contract decision this accessor forces.

findPersonByName.purpose: Search for people by name within a group, used when adding a person to a record or linking them into a whakapapa.
findPersonByName.reason: Real requirement with no equivalent elsewhere. Flag as an adapter risk rather than a data-model problem: Holochain needs an explicit index or anchor to support name search, and nostr has no server-side text search at all. A good early test of whether the contract can express a capability a backend may decline.

deletePerson.purpose: Remove a person from the record, tombstoning both their profile and the whakapapa links that reference them.
deletePerson.reason: Genuine requirement, highest call-site count in the domain (14). Named deletePerson but resolves to tombstoneProfileAndLinks - the name lies about the semantics and the contract should use the honest one. Deletion is where the three protocols diverge hardest: SSB tombstones, Holochain deletes with a retained source-chain record, nostr sends a request relays may ignore. The contract must not promise erasure it cannot deliver.

loadPersonList.purpose: List the people in a tribe, with an admin variant returning the fuller record available to kaitiaki.
loadPersonList.reason: The only multi-variant accessor in the corpus - it selects between LIST_ADMIN_PERSON and LIST_PERSON on a runtime argument. That conditional is a permission decision made in the frontend, which is exactly wrong for a backend-agnostic contract: the backend should decide what the caller may see. Keep the capability, but expose one listPeople operation and let the adapter vary the response by the caller's actual rights.

getWhakapapaView.purpose: Open a saved whakapapa view - the curated lens over the graph: which person is the focus, which profiles are ignored, which parent or partner counts as primary where someone has several, plus the view's name, image and guardians.
getWhakapapaView.reason: Core read of the core domain. Worth stating plainly because the name misleads: a WhakapapaView is not the tree, it is a saved lens over it. The graph itself is the links. Keeping that distinction explicit in the contract matters - view metadata (focus, ignoredProfiles, importantRelationships) is pure application state and ports to any backend unchanged, whereas the links underneath are where the protocols actually differ.

getWhakapapaViews.purpose: List the whakapapa views belonging to a group, for the index screen and for choosing a target when submitting a change.
getWhakapapaViews.reason: Shares WhakapapaFragment with getWhakapapaView, so the record type is common, but this differs by cardinality and selection criteria rather than by projection - the confirmed merge test does not apply. Four call sites including the index view.

saveWhakapapaView.purpose: Create or update a whakapapa view - naming it, setting its focus, ignoring profiles, or recording which relationships are primary.
saveWhakapapaView.reason: Irreducible write, no SSB flags, five call sites. Carries the same unsettled write-acknowledgement question as savePerson. The payload is application state rather than protocol state, so this is one of the accessors most likely to port cleanly.

getDescendantLinks.purpose: Fetch the child and partner links descending from a person, to draw the tree below them.
getDescendantLinks.reason: Distinct graph walk, so it is kept rather than merged with getFamilyLinks despite the identical return shape - they differ by concern, not projection. Record for Milestone 2: this and getFamilyLinks are the sharpest test of backend agnosticism in the whole corpus. Holochain can traverse via get_links but needs the walk written into a zome; nostr has no server-side traversal at all, so a descendant walk becomes fetch-all-links plus a client-side walk. If the contract must express traversal as a filter rather than a walk, that changes frontend code, not just the adapter - which would put pressure on Leg 2's zero-frontend-changes metric.

getFamilyLinks.purpose: Fetch the links around a person - immediate family, or extended kin when asked - to draw their local whakapapa.
getFamilyLinks.reason: Same return shape as getDescendantLinks but a different walk, and already parameterised by depth via `extended`. That existing parameter is evidence the contract could express traversal as one operation with a mode rather than one operation per walk; noting it for Milestone 2 rather than merging now, since collapsing two graph walks is a contract design decision, not a triage call.

whakapapaLink.purpose: Look up a single link between two people, checking whether a parent-child or partner relationship already exists before creating one.
whakapapaLink.reason: Point lookup on an edge, used to avoid duplicate links. Carries recps directly rather than via a fragment, so per-edge visibility is a real requirement, not inherited noise - a whakapapa link can be more sensitive than either person on its end. Any adapter has to answer who may see a given relationship, and this accessor is where that surfaces most cheaply.

saveLink.purpose: Create or update a link between two people - the act of recording a relationship in the whakapapa.
saveLink.reason: The fundamental write of the application: whakapapa is the links. Four call sites across dialogs, stories and the tree store. No SSB flags on the mutation itself, but it is the operation whose permission semantics matter most, since creating a link asserts a relationship between two people who may have different guardians.

getSubmissions.purpose: List the pending proposals awaiting review - what a kaitiaki sees when deciding what to approve, including each proposal's target, comments, group and dependencies.
getSubmissions.reason: The only read in the domain and the entry point to the whole approval workflow. Two things to carry into Milestone 2. First, it takes no arguments at all: no group filter, no status filter, no pagination. That is affordable when a server holds the index and cheap to query, but on Holochain it means an anchor plus a walk, and on nostr it means fetching a lot of events and filtering client-side. Second, it carries six SSB flags, all inherited through SubmissionFragment and its nested community and profile fragments, so the coupling belongs to those fragments and should be decided there once. An earlier crutRevision flag on this accessor was a false positive from the word conflict in a pasted error comment, now fixed in the scanner - there is no CRUT revision handling in the frontend.

proposeNewGroupPerson.purpose: Propose adding a new person to a group, for a kaitiaki to review.
proposeNewGroupPerson.reason: Typed proposal write. The propose family exists because contributors without write rights still need a path to contribute - that is a real requirement of the sovereignty model, not an SSB artefact, and every candidate backend must express it somehow.

proposeEditGroupPerson.purpose: Propose changes to an existing person's profile within a group.
proposeEditGroupPerson.reason: Typed proposal write, distinct payload from proposeNewGroupPerson because it targets an existing profileId. Pairs with approveEditGroupPersonSubmission.

proposeEditWhakapapaView.purpose: Propose changes to a whakapapa view - its focus, name, or which relationships are treated as primary.
proposeEditWhakapapaView.reason: Typed proposal write over view metadata rather than over people or links. Since view metadata is pure application state, this is among the proposals most likely to port unchanged.

proposeNewWhakapapaLink.purpose: Propose a new relationship between two people, for review before it enters the whakapapa.
proposeNewWhakapapaLink.reason: Typed proposal write over a graph edge. Carries the same sensitivity noted on whakapapaLink: asserting a relationship involves two people who may have different guardians, so who may propose and who may approve are not necessarily the same question.

proposeTombstone.purpose: Propose removing a record, for a kaitiaki to review rather than deleting it outright.
proposeTombstone.reason: Proposal-to-delete, distinct from both rejectSubmission and tombstoneSubmission. Inherits the deletion divergence recorded on deletePerson: the three candidate protocols disagree on what removal means, so a proposal to remove needs the contract to say what approving it actually guarantees.

approveSubmission.purpose: Approve a proposal wholesale, accepting it as submitted.
approveSubmission.reason: Distinct from the typed approve family: it takes targetId rather than allowedFields, so it approves the proposal as a whole instead of field by field. Single call site. Worth confirming during Milestone 2 whether wholesale approval is still wanted, or whether it is a superseded earlier form of the typed accessors.

approveEditGroupPersonSubmission.purpose: Approve a proposed edit to a person's profile, accepting only the fields the reviewer allows.
approveEditGroupPersonSubmission.reason: Part of the typed approve family, all four of which share the identical signature ({id, comment, allowedFields}) and differ only in payload type and which mutation they name. Kept rather than merged: the payloads are genuinely different types, which is a concern difference, not a projection one. But record for Milestone 2 that the frontend is dispatching on the submission's targetType - a field the backend already holds - which is the same inversion loadPersonList shows. A contract could express this as one approve operation over a discriminated payload and let the backend route it. The allowedFields argument is field-level approval: a kaitiaki accepts some proposed changes and not others. That is the finest-grained permission in the application and the hardest to port. GraphQL-over-SSB enforces it server-side; Holochain could validate it in a zome; nostr cannot enforce it at all, since nothing stops a client publishing an approval event. Treat this as a capability the contract must let a backend decline rather than silently fake.

approveEditWhakapapaViewSubmission.purpose: Approve a proposed edit to a whakapapa view, accepting only the fields the reviewer allows.
approveEditWhakapapaViewSubmission.reason: Part of the typed approve family, all four of which share the identical signature ({id, comment, allowedFields}) and differ only in payload type and which mutation they name. Kept rather than merged: the payloads are genuinely different types, which is a concern difference, not a projection one. But record for Milestone 2 that the frontend is dispatching on the submission's targetType - a field the backend already holds - which is the same inversion loadPersonList shows. A contract could express this as one approve operation over a discriminated payload and let the backend route it.

approveNewGroupPersonSubmission.purpose: Approve adding a proposed new person to a group.
approveNewGroupPersonSubmission.reason: Part of the typed approve family, all four of which share the identical signature ({id, comment, allowedFields}) and differ only in payload type and which mutation they name. Kept rather than merged: the payloads are genuinely different types, which is a concern difference, not a projection one. But record for Milestone 2 that the frontend is dispatching on the submission's targetType - a field the backend already holds - which is the same inversion loadPersonList shows. A contract could express this as one approve operation over a discriminated payload and let the backend route it. Its store action also performs follow-on work beyond the mutation, so the call site is not a thin pass-through - check what else must happen on approval before treating this as a pure write.

approveNewWhakapapaLink.purpose: Approve a proposed new relationship, admitting it into the whakapapa.
approveNewWhakapapaLink.reason: Part of the typed approve family, all four of which share the identical signature ({id, comment, allowedFields}) and differ only in payload type and which mutation they name. Kept rather than merged: the payloads are genuinely different types, which is a concern difference, not a projection one. But record for Milestone 2 that the frontend is dispatching on the submission's targetType - a field the backend already holds - which is the same inversion loadPersonList shows. A contract could express this as one approve operation over a discriminated payload and let the backend route it. Note the naming inconsistency: the other three carry a Submission suffix and this one does not. Use one convention in the contract.

rejectSubmission.purpose: Decline a proposal, with a comment explaining why.
rejectSubmission.reason: Irreducible counterpart to approval, and distinct from tombstoneSubmission - declining a proposal leaves it visible with its reasoning, which matters when the proposer is a community member who deserves an answer. Keep that distinction explicit in the contract rather than collapsing reject and remove.

tombstoneSubmission.purpose: Remove a submission from view entirely, rather than declining it on the record.
tombstoneSubmission.reason: Different concern from rejectSubmission: removal rather than refusal. Three call sites. Carries the same unresolved deletion semantics as deletePerson and proposeTombstone - all three need one answer about what removal guarantees, decided once rather than per accessor.

createSubmissionsLink.purpose: Record that one proposal depends on another, so related changes are reviewed and applied in the right order.
createSubmissionsLink.reason: Least obvious accessor in the domain and easy to mistake for whakapapa link creation - it links submissions to each other, not people. Proposals form dependency chains, which getSubmissions reads back as `dependencies`. Any backend must preserve ordering between dependent proposals; on a protocol with no ordering guarantees between events, that is a real constraint and not merely a convenience.

saveSettings.purpose: Create or update a group's settings - the per-tribe configuration a kaitiaki controls.
saveSettings.reason: Irreducible write. Carries the same unsettled write-acknowledgement question as savePerson and saveWhakapapaView; decide that shape once across all three.

getSettings.reason: Selects recps directly rather than inheriting it, so per-group settings visibility is a real requirement. Settings can be more sensitive than the group they configure, since they may encode who holds authority.

getAllSettings.purpose: Read settings across every group the user belongs to, for screens that span groups.
getAllSettings.reason: Differs from getSettings by cardinality and selection criteria, not by projection, so the confirmed merge test does not apply. Also carries recps directly. Like getSubmissions it takes no filter, so the fan-out question applies here too on a backend without a server-held index.

deleteSettings.reason: Keep the capability, but record the shape: this is not a delete at all - it resolves to saveSettings with a tombstone payload. That is append-only semantics leaking into the accessor set, and it is why the domain shows two accessors pointing at one mutation. On a backend with real deletes these are genuinely different operations, so the contract should express delete as delete and let each adapter decide whether it implements that as a write. Same family as deletePerson, proposeTombstone and tombstoneSubmission - one deletion answer, applied consistently.

getBackup.purpose: Retrieve the user's identity backup, so they can recover their account on another device or after reinstalling.
getBackup.reason: The need is universal and non-negotiable - losing identity means losing access to whakapapa - but the artefact is protocol-specific: an SSB feed keypair, a Holochain agent key, a nostr nsec. The contract should express this as export-my-identity and leave the format to the adapter, never as a typed key structure. Three call sites.

deleteAhau.purpose: Delete the local database and reset the application.
deleteAhau.reason: Genuine capability with two call sites. Protocol-neutral as an intent, entirely protocol-specific in effect: what remains afterwards, and what other peers already hold, differs sharply between a replicated SSB log, a Holochain source chain, and events already accepted by nostr relays. The contract must be honest that this is local reset, not erasure - the same distinction flagged on deletePerson.

updateAutoPrune.purpose: Configure automatic pruning of cached remote blobs - how often, after what delay, above what size.
updateAutoPrune.reason: Configures ssb-hyper-blobs auto-pruning - startDelay, maxRemoteSize, intervalTime - which is administration of an SSB storage subsystem, not a whakapapa requirement. Holochain has no hyper-blobs; nostr has no blob storage at all and pushes media to external hosts. Putting this in a backend-agnostic contract would make the contract an SSB admin panel. Drop the operation, but note the user need behind it survives: StorageSettings.vue is a real screen where someone manages how much disk Ahau uses. Whether v2 offers that at all, and in whose terms, is a cut-list decision for Leg 2 - it cannot be expressed until a backend is chosen, because the units differ entirely.

disableAutoPrune.reason: Configures ssb-hyper-blobs auto-pruning - startDelay, maxRemoteSize, intervalTime - which is administration of an SSB storage subsystem, not a whakapapa requirement. Holochain has no hyper-blobs; nostr has no blob storage at all and pushes media to external hosts. Putting this in a backend-agnostic contract would make the contract an SSB admin panel. Drop the operation, but note the user need behind it survives: StorageSettings.vue is a real screen where someone manages how much disk Ahau uses. Whether v2 offers that at all, and in whose terms, is a cut-list decision for Leg 2 - it cannot be expressed until a backend is chosen, because the units differ entirely.

getAutoPruneConfig.purpose: Read the current automatic blob pruning configuration.
getAutoPruneConfig.reason: Configures ssb-hyper-blobs auto-pruning - startDelay, maxRemoteSize, intervalTime - which is administration of an SSB storage subsystem, not a whakapapa requirement. Holochain has no hyper-blobs; nostr has no blob storage at all and pushes media to external hosts. Putting this in a backend-agnostic contract would make the contract an SSB admin panel. Drop the operation, but note the user need behind it survives: StorageSettings.vue is a real screen where someone manages how much disk Ahau uses. Whether v2 offers that at all, and in whose terms, is a cut-list decision for Leg 2 - it cannot be expressed until a backend is chosen, because the units differ entirely.

getTribe.purpose: Read one group - its public and private profile, who tends it, and the user's standing in it.
getTribe.reason: Core read. Four SSB flags, all inherited through the community and profile fragments, so the coupling belongs to those fragments and should be settled there once rather than per accessor.

getTribes.purpose: List the groups the user belongs to, for navigation and group switching.
getTribes.reason: Differs from getTribe by cardinality, not projection, so the merge test does not apply. Four call sites.

initGroup.purpose: Create a new group - the act that establishes a tribe or community and the permission boundary everything else in Ahau hangs off.
initGroup.reason: Irreducible write and the root of the permission model - everything else in this domain hangs off a group existing. Under SSB this establishes a keyring; under Holochain it would be a DNA or membrane decision; under nostr there is no group primitive at all. Likely the single hardest operation to port, and worth being the first thing a Leg 2 adapter attempts.

addAdminsToGroup.purpose: Grant administrative rights over a group to named people.
addAdminsToGroup.reason: Explicit permission grant, and the clearest statement in the corpus of what the application means by authority. Holochain can express this as capability grants validated in a zome; nostr cannot express it at all. A capability the contract must let a backend decline rather than fake.

getMembers.purpose: List the people in a group.
getMembers.reason: Named getMembers but resolves to listGroupAuthors - under SSB, group membership is feed authorship. That equivalence is an SSB artefact, not a requirement: membership and having-written-something are different ideas, and a member who has never posted still belongs. The contract should ask for members and let the adapter decide how it knows, rather than inheriting authorship as the definition.

createSubGroup.purpose: Create a subgroup within a group, for a hapu or whanau within a wider iwi.
createSubGroup.reason: Real structural requirement reflecting how the communities Ahau serves are actually organised. Inherits the group-creation portability problem recorded on initGroup, plus nesting.

getSubGroups.purpose: List the subgroups of a group.
getSubGroups.reason: Core read for navigating nested community structure. Four inherited SSB flags via fragments, same fragment-level decision as getTribe.

deleteSubGroup.purpose: Remove a person's membership of a subgroup, and their corresponding record in the parent group.
deleteSubGroup.reason: Named deleteSubGroup but it does not delete a subgroup - it tombstones a profile in the subgroup and its counterpart in the parent group. The name is wrong twice over, and the contract should use honest names. Issues two writes inside one GraphQL operation, aliased over saveCommunity, because an Ahau group is a paired record: a discoverable public profile and a members-only private one. Record for Milestone 2 as an atomicity question the contract must answer. GraphQL gives the pairing for free in one request; Holochain can commit both entries in a single zome call and get atomicity; nostr publishes two independent events with no atomicity whatsoever, so a client can crash between them and leave a group half-updated or half-deleted. The contract has to state whether paired writes are atomic, and an adapter that cannot guarantee it must say so rather than pretend.

saveCommunity.purpose: Create or update a group's profile.
saveCommunity.reason: Absorbs savePublicCommunity. Four call sites, the most used write in the domain.

savePublicCommunity.purpose: Create or update the publicly discoverable part of a group's profile.
savePublicCommunity.reason: Identical mutation to saveCommunity. The only differences are client-side: it prunes the input against PERMITTED_PUBLIC_COMMUNITY_ATTRS instead of PERMITTED_COMMUNITY_ATTRS, and sets allowPublic. That is one operation with a different payload prepared in the frontend, not two operations. Merging carries a condition: the public/private distinction is real and must survive as an explicit visibility argument on the contract. Note also that the field allowlist is enforced by a client-side prune() call, so it is not enforcement at all - a modified client can write whatever it likes. Tolerable against a trusted local SSB server, much less so against a shared backend. Same pattern appears in person-helpers with PERMITTED_PERSON_ATTRS.

updateTribe.purpose: Update both halves of a group's paired profile at once.
updateTribe.reason: Distinct from saveCommunity because it writes the public and private records together rather than one of them. Issues two writes inside one GraphQL operation, aliased over saveCommunity, because an Ahau group is a paired record: a discoverable public profile and a members-only private one. Record for Milestone 2 as an atomicity question the contract must answer. GraphQL gives the pairing for free in one request; Holochain can commit both entries in a single zome call and get atomicity; nostr publishes two independent events with no atomicity whatsoever, so a client can crash between them and leave a group half-updated or half-deleted. The contract has to state whether paired writes are atomic, and an adapter that cannot guarantee it must say so rather than pretend.

deleteTribe.purpose: Remove a group, tombstoning both its public and private records.
deleteTribe.reason: Keep the capability; the shape needs work. Like deleteSettings this is not a delete but a save carrying a tombstone, which is append-only semantics surfacing in the accessor set. Issues two writes inside one GraphQL operation, aliased over saveCommunity, because an Ahau group is a paired record: a discoverable public profile and a members-only private one. Record for Milestone 2 as an atomicity question the contract must answer. GraphQL gives the pairing for free in one request; Holochain can commit both entries in a single zome call and get atomicity; nostr publishes two independent events with no atomicity whatsoever, so a client can crash between them and leave a group half-updated or half-deleted. The contract has to state whether paired writes are atomic, and an adapter that cannot guarantee it must say so rather than pretend.

getCommunity.purpose: Read a single community by id.
getCommunity.reason: No call sites anywhere in ui/src - one of only three unused accessors in the corpus. Its job is covered by getTribe, which is used and returns more. Dropping dead code is the cheapest possible reduction in contract surface; carrying it forward would mean an adapter implementing an operation nothing calls.

getStory.purpose: Open a single story - a record of an event, with its text, media, contributors and the people it mentions.
getStory.reason: Core read of the archive. Four SSB flags, all inherited through STORY_FRAGMENT and the profile fragments beneath it, so the coupling belongs to those fragments and should be decided there once.

getAllStories.purpose: List the stories in the archive for browsing.
getAllStories.reason: Differs from getStory by cardinality, not projection. No filter or pagination argument, so the unbounded fan-out concern first recorded on getSubmissions applies here too - and the archive is the collection most likely to grow large.

getAllStoriesByMentions.purpose: Find the stories that mention a given person, so someone's record shows where they appear in the wider archive.
getAllStoriesByMentions.reason: Reverse lookup, and the root field is person rather than stories - it traverses from a person to the stories referencing them. Worth flagging for Milestone 2 alongside the whakapapa traversal accessors: this is another server-side walk. Of the three candidate protocols nostr is unusually well suited here, since tag-based filtering is exactly what relays do; Holochain needs explicit links. A useful counter-example to the assumption that nostr is always the weaker backend.

saveStory.reason: Irreducible write. Same unsettled write-acknowledgement shape as savePerson, saveWhakapapaView and saveSettings - one decision covering all of them.

deleteStory.purpose: Remove a story from the archive.
deleteStory.reason: Another delete implemented as a save carrying a tombstone, which is why this domain shows two accessors pointing at one mutation. Append-only semantics surfacing in the accessor set. Keep the capability; the contract should express delete as delete and let each adapter decide whether it implements that as a write.

getCollection.purpose: Open a single collection - a curated grouping of stories.
getCollection.reason: Filed under story only because it lives in lib/story-helpers.mjs, while saveCollection, deleteCollection and getAllCollections live in the collection module. The source split is inconsistent and the contract should group all four together. Worth noting that domain in this inventory is derived from file path, so it reports where code lives rather than what it concerns - accurate, but it makes this kind of misfiling visible.

saveArtefact.purpose: Create or update an artefact - an image, recording or document held in the archive.
saveArtefact.reason: Irreducible write, and the one most tied to blob handling. Media storage differs completely across the candidates: SSB has hyper-blobs, Holochain has no blob store designed for large media, and nostr pushes media to external hosts entirely. Expect this accessor to need a capability the contract lets an adapter satisfy differently, rather than a single uniform implementation.

DELETE_ARTEFACT.purpose: Remove an artefact from the archive.
DELETE_ARTEFACT.reason: Keep the capability, fix the name: this is a function named in SHOUT_CASE as though it were a gql constant, the only accessor in the corpus breaking that convention. The contract should call it deleteArtefact. Another delete implemented as a save carrying a tombstone, which is why this domain shows two accessors pointing at one mutation. Append-only semantics surfacing in the accessor set. Keep the capability; the contract should express delete as delete and let each adapter decide whether it implements that as a write.

getArtefact.purpose: Read a single artefact by id.
getArtefact.reason: No call sites anywhere in ui/src. One of the three unused accessors in the corpus, and two of those three are in this domain - the artefact read path appears to have been superseded, with stories and collections carrying their artefacts inline through fragments instead. Dropping dead code is the cheapest reduction in contract surface available.

getArtefacts.reason: No call sites anywhere in ui/src, same superseded read path as getArtefact. If v2 later needs an artefact browser it should be specified against that requirement rather than resurrected from an operation nothing called.

saveCollection.purpose: Create or update a collection - a curated grouping of stories.
saveCollection.reason: Irreducible write. Collections are pure application state, so this is among the operations most likely to port unchanged.

deleteCollection.reason: Another delete implemented as a save carrying a tombstone, which is why this domain shows two accessors pointing at one mutation. Append-only semantics surfacing in the accessor set. Keep the capability; the contract should express delete as delete and let each adapter decide whether it implements that as a write.

saveCollectionStoryLink.purpose: Add a story to a collection, or remove it.
saveCollectionStoryLink.reason: Edge write between two application records, structurally similar to saveLink but without the sensitivity: a collection membership asserts curation, not kinship. Should port straightforwardly wherever links can be expressed.

getAllCollections.purpose: List the collections available for browsing.
getAllCollections.reason: Core read. Carries feedId and originalAuthor via fragments rather than directly, so the provenance coupling is inherited and belongs to the fragment decision.

createGroupApplication.reason: Entry point to membership and a genuine requirement of the sovereignty model - people must be able to ask, and kaitiaki must be able to decide. Note for Milestone 2 that this is a second approval workflow running parallel to submissions, with its own propose, accept and decline verbs. Whether the contract expresses one review mechanism or two is a consolidation question worth answering deliberately rather than inheriting.

acceptGroupApplication.purpose: Admit an applicant to a group.
acceptGroupApplication.reason: The write that actually confers membership, and therefore the operation most in need of backend enforcement. Holochain can validate it in a zome; nostr cannot enforce membership at all. Pairs with addAdminsToGroup as the core of the permission model.

declineGroupApplication.reason: Counterpart to accept, and distinct from it in the same way rejectSubmission is distinct from tombstoneSubmission - a decision on the record rather than a silent removal.

listGroupApplications.purpose: List applications awaiting a decision, so a kaitiaki can see who is asking to join.
listGroupApplications.reason: Named listGroupApplications but the root field is unseen, so the operation is really the unreviewed subset rather than all applications. Another name that does not describe what it fetches; the contract should be explicit about whether it returns pending items or everything. Carries five SSB flags via fragments, the densest coupling outside whoami and getSubmissions.

offerMembershipCredential.purpose: Issue a verifiable credential attesting that someone belongs to a group.
offerMembershipCredential.reason: Resolves to offerCredential and takes feedId directly, binding a portable credential to an SSB feed identity. The credential idea is protocol-independent and genuinely useful - it is the one mechanism here that could outlive any particular backend - but the binding must move to a backend-neutral identity. Whether v2 carries credentials at all is a Leg 2 cut-list decision; the triage question is only whether this is a real requirement, and it is.

getAllCredentials.purpose: List the verifiable credentials the user holds.
getAllCredentials.reason: Three call sites and a wallet UI behind it. No SSB flags at all - one of the cleanest accessors in the corpus, because W3C verifiable credentials are already a protocol-independent format. Its portability is a point in its favour, though whether v2 keeps the wallet is for the Leg 2 cut list, not for triage.

getIndexes.purpose: Report whether the backend has finished preparing data, and how far along it is, so the app knows when it can render.
getIndexes.reason: Kept despite being the most SSB-internal read in the corpus, because dropping it would leave the frontend with no way to know when the backend is usable - main.js currently polls GraphQL at startup for exactly this. The capability is required of every adapter. The shape is not: isIndexing, isRebuilding, percentageIndexed and percentageIndexedSinceStartup are ssb-db2 internals with no counterpart in a Holochain conductor or a nostr relay. Express as backend readiness, with progress optional and a backend free to report only ready or not-ready.

getPatakas.purpose: List the storehouses replicating this user's groups.
getPatakas.reason: Pataka are the storehouses that hold and replicate a group's records - an iwi running its own always-on node rather than trusting someone else's. The concept is central to what Ahau means by data sovereignty and must survive, which is why this is kept rather than dropped alongside the hyper-blobs pruning accessors. The shape must not survive: these operations are keyed on feedId as the peer's identity, and replication itself works completely differently across the candidates. Holochain has always-on nodes and its own gossip; nostr's nearest analogue is a relay, which you choose rather than block, and which holds events rather than replicating a peer's log. Express this as trusted-storehouse management with a backend-neutral peer identity, and expect each adapter to mean something quite different by it.

getProfile.purpose: Read a community profile - how a person or group presents itself within a group, as distinct from their node in the whakapapa.
getProfile.reason: Ten call sites, the second most used read in the corpus after whoami. Deliberately not merged with getPerson despite the overlap: they query different root fields and mean different things - a person is a node in the whakapapa, a profile is how an identity appears within a group. The distinction is load-bearing for the permission model, since the same person can appear differently in different groups, and collapsing it would lose that. Four SSB flags, inherited via fragments.
